questions.explain: Sum = 82 + 88 + 91 + 79 = 340. Average = 340 ÷ 4 = 85. (340 is the total, not the average.)

questions.text: The sum of three consecutive integers is 96. What is the largest of the three?
questions.explain: The middle integer is 96 ÷ 3 = 32, so the integers are 31, 32, and 33. The largest is 33.
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: A worker earns $16 per hour, with time-and-a-half for every hour over 40 in a week. How much does she earn for working 48 hours?
questions.explain: Regular pay: 40 × $16 = $640. Overtime rate: 1.5 × $16 = $24. Overtime pay: 8 × $24 = $192. Total: $832.
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: On a map, 1 inch represents 40 miles. Two towns are 234 inches apart on the map. What is the actual distance between them?
questions.explain: 2.75 × 40 = 110 miles.

questions.text: A bag contains 6 red marbles, 3 green marbles, and 1 blue marble. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is NOT red?
questions.explain: There are 10 marbles, and 4 of them are not red (3 green + 1 blue). P = 410 = 25. (35 is the probability that it IS red.)
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: A room measures 12 feet by 18 feet. Carpet costs $27 per square yard. How much will it cost to carpet the room?
questions.explain: Area = 12 × 18 = 216 square feet. 1 square yard = 9 square feet, so 216 ÷ 9 = 24 square yards. Cost = 24 × $27 = $648. ($5,832 comes from forgetting to convert to square yards.)
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: Maria is 4 times as old as her daughter. In 6 years, Maria will be 3 times as old as her daughter. How old is the daughter now?
questions.explain: Let d = daughter's age now; Maria = 4d. In 6 years: 4d + 6 = 3(d + 6) → 4d + 6 = 3d + 18 → d = 12. Check: Maria is 48; in 6 years, 54 = 3 × 18. ✓
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: A pair of boots costs $240 and is on sale for 25% off. A 6% sales tax is charged on the sale price. What is the total cost?
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: After a 20% discount, a jacket costs $64. What was the original price?
questions.explain: $64 is 80% of the original price, so the original = $64 ÷ 0.80 = $80. ($76.80 comes from wrongly adding 20% of $64.)
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: Two trucks leave the same depot at the same time and drive in opposite directions, one at 45 mph and the other at 55 mph. After how many hours will they be 350 miles apart?
questions.explain: Moving apart, their speeds add: 45 + 55 = 100 mph. Time = 350 ÷ 100 = 3.5 hours.
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: A driver travels 120 miles to a training site at 60 mph and returns the same way at 40 mph. What is the average speed for the whole round trip?
questions.explain: Time going: 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours. Time returning: 120 ÷ 40 = 3 hours. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 mph. (50 mph is the trap of averaging the two speeds.)
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: Thirty coins, all dimes and quarters, are worth $4.80 in total. How many of the coins are quarters?
questions.explain: Test the choices: 12 quarters = $3.00 and 18 dimes = $1.80; $3.00 + $1.80 = $4.80. ✓ So 12 are quarters (18 is the number of dimes).
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: A 30-pound mix of peanuts and cashews sells for $3 per pound. Peanuts cost $2 per pound and cashews cost $5 per pound. How many pounds of cashews are in the mix?
questions.explain: Let c = pounds of cashews. 5c + 2(30 − c) = 90 → 3c + 60 = 90 → c = 10. (20 pounds is the amount of peanuts.)
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: An inlet pipe can fill a tank in 3 hours. A drain can empty the full tank in 6 hours. If the tank starts empty and both are open, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.explain: The drain works against the pipe, so subtract rates: 13 − 16 = 26 − 16 = 16 tank per hour. The tank fills in 6 hours. (2 hours would be correct only if both were filling.)
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: In a platoon, 12 soldiers averaged 82 on a test and the other 18 soldiers averaged 92. What was the average score for all 30 soldiers?
questions.explain: Total points: 12 × 82 + 18 × 92 = 984 + 1,656 = 2,640. Average = 2,640 ÷ 30 = 88. (87 is the simple average of 82 and 92, which ignores that more soldiers scored 92.)
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: A unit grew from 1,200 members to 1,500 members. What was the percent increase?
questions.explain: Increase = 300. Divide by the original number: 300 ÷ 1,200 = 0.25 = 25%. (20% comes from dividing by 1,500.)
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: A 6-foot-tall soldier casts a 4-foot shadow. At the same time, a flagpole casts a 22-foot shadow. How tall is the flagpole?
questions.explain: Height and shadow are proportional: 64 = x22 → 4x = 132 → x = 33 feet. (The soldier is 1.5 times as tall as his shadow, so the pole is 1.5 × 22.)
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: A drawer contains 4 black socks and 6 white socks. Two socks are pulled out at random, one after the other, without replacing the first. What is the probability that both are black?
questions.explain: First draw: 410. Second draw (one black sock is gone): 39. Multiply: 410 × 39 = 1290 = 215. (425 would be the answer with replacement.)
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: A water tank is shaped like a box 5 feet long, 4 feet wide, and 3 feet high. If 1 cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons, about how many gallons does the tank hold?
questions.explain: Volume = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 cubic feet. 60 × 7.5 = 450 gallons.
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: One alarm sounds every 8 minutes and another sounds every 12 minutes. Both sound at 0900. When will they next sound at the same time?
questions.explain: They line up at the least common multiple of 8 and 12, which is 24 minutes. 0900 + 24 minutes = 0924.
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: A patrol leaves at 0945 and returns at 1520. How long was the patrol gone?
questions.explain: 0945 to 1445 is 5 hours. 1445 to 1520 is 35 minutes. Total: 5 hours 35 minutes.
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: A salesperson earns a base salary of $500 per month plus a 6% commission on all sales over $10,000. How much does she earn in a month with $24,000 in sales?
questions.explain: Commission applies only to sales over $10,000: $24,000 − $10,000 = $14,000. Commission: 0.06 × $14,000 = $840. Total: $500 + $840 = $1,340.
questions.instr: Solve each problem. Use scratch paper; no calculator.

questions.text: The price of a rifle scope rose 20% and then fell 20%. How does the final price compare with the original price?
questions.explain: Use $100: up 20% → $120; down 20% of $120 = $24 → $96. That is 4% lower. The second 20% is taken from a bigger number.

questions.text: Car A leaves a base at 8:00 a.m. traveling 50 mph. Car B leaves the same base at 9:00 a.m. on the same road traveling 70 mph. At what time will Car B catch up to Car A?
questions.explain: At 9:00, Car A is 50 miles ahead. Car B gains 70 − 50 = 20 mph. Time to catch up: 50 ÷ 20 = 2.5 hours after 9:00 → 11:30 a.m.
questions.instr: These are harder, multi-step problems like the ones the computer test gives to strong test-takers.

questions.text: How many liters of a 20% acid solution must be added to 10 liters of a 50% acid solution to make a 30% acid solution?
questions.explain: Acid amounts: 0.20x + 0.50(10) = 0.30(x + 10) → 0.20x + 5 = 0.30x + 3 → 2 = 0.10x → x = 20 liters. Check: 4 + 5 = 9 liters of acid in 30 liters = 30%. ✓

questions.text: The average of five numbers is 24. When one of the numbers is removed, the average of the remaining four numbers is 21. What number was removed?
questions.explain: Total of five: 5 × 24 = 120. Total of four: 4 × 21 = 84. Removed number: 120 − 84 = 36.

questions.text: A crew of 6 workers can build a bunker in 10 days. Working at the same rate, how many days would it take a crew of 15 workers?
questions.explain: The job takes 6 × 10 = 60 worker-days. With 15 workers: 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days. More workers means fewer days, so 25 cannot be right.

questions.text: $5,000 is deposited in an account that earns 6% interest compounded once a year. How much is in the account after 2 years?
questions.explain: After year 1: $5,000 × 1.06 = $5,300. After year 2: $5,300 × 1.06 = $5,618. ($5,600 is simple interest, which ignores interest on the first year's interest.)

questions.text: The ratio of sailors to Marines aboard a ship is 5:3. There are 120 Marines aboard. How many sailors and Marines are aboard in all?

questions.text: A battalion has 800 soldiers. 40% are on leave. Of the soldiers who are not on leave, 25% are in training. How many soldiers are neither on leave nor in training?
questions.explain: Not on leave: 60% of 800 = 480. In training: 25% of 480 = 120. Neither: 480 − 120 = 360. (Taking 25% of 800 instead of 480 leads to 280.)

questions.text: A runner completes 3 laps of a 400-meter track in 4 minutes 30 seconds. What is the runner's average speed, in meters per second?
questions.explain: Distance: 3 × 400 = 1,200 meters. Time: 4 min 30 s = 270 seconds. Speed = 1,200 ÷ 270 ≈ 4.44 meters per second.

questions.text: In 5 years, John will be twice as old as he was 10 years ago. How old is John now?
questions.explain: J + 5 = 2(J − 10) → J + 5 = 2J − 20 → J = 25. Check: in 5 years he is 30; 10 years ago he was 15; 30 = 2 × 15. ✓

questions.text: Which of these is the best buy?
questions.explain: Unit prices: $3.00 ÷ 12 = $0.25 per ounce; $3.84 ÷ 16 = $0.24; $7.36 ÷ 32 = $0.23; $4.40 ÷ 20 = $0.22 per ounce — the lowest. The biggest package is not always the best buy.

questions.text: Two standard six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability that the numbers rolled add up to 7?
questions.explain: There are 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely outcomes. Six of them total 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1). P = 636 = 16.

questions.text: A truck uses 18 gallons of fuel to travel 270 miles. At this rate, how many gallons will it use to travel 450 miles?

questions.explain: SA = 2(4 × 5) + 2(4 × 6) + 2(5 × 6) = 40 + 48 + 60 = 148 cm². (120 cm³ would be the volume.)

questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: An element's atomic number is equal to the number of:
questions.explain: The atomic number is the number of protons. Protons plus neutrons is the mass number.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which of the following is a chemical change?
questions.explain: Rusting creates a new substance (iron oxide). The others change only form or appearance.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A substance with a pH of 3 is:
questions.explain: Any pH below 7 is acidic. Vinegar and lemon juice have pH values near 2 or 3.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.explain: Sodium's symbol is Na, from its Latin name natrium. S is sulfur.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Water (H2O) is an example of a(n):
questions.explain: Water is two elements — hydrogen and oxygen — chemically combined in a fixed ratio, so it is a compound.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: The change of a solid directly into a gas, without becoming a liquid first, is called:
questions.explain: Sublimation is solid → gas, as when dry ice "smokes." Deposition is the reverse (gas → solid).
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: The same force pushes two carts. Cart A has twice the mass of Cart B. Compared with Cart B, Cart A will have:
questions.explain: From F = ma, a = F ÷ m. With twice the mass, the same force gives half the acceleration.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A rocket moves forward because its engines push exhaust gases backward. This is an example of:
choices: the law of conservation of mass.
questions.explain: Newton's third law: for every action (gases pushed backward) there is an equal and opposite reaction (rocket pushed forward).
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What kind of energy does a stretched rubber band have?
questions.explain: A stretched rubber band stores energy, so it has potential energy. When released, the energy becomes kinetic (motion).
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Heat from the Sun reaches Earth through the vacuum of space by:
questions.explain: Conduction and convection need matter. Only radiation (electromagnetic waves) travels through empty space.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Sound travels fastest through which of the following?
questions.explain: Sound travels fastest through solids like steel, slower through liquids, slowest through gases, and not at all through a vacuum.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which color of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.explain: In ROY G BIV, red has the longest wavelength and violet has the shortest.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: The bending of light as it passes from air into water is called:
questions.explain: Refraction is the bending of light when it moves from one material into another.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: An astronaut's mass on the Moon is:
choices: one-sixth of her mass on Earth.
six times her mass on Earth.
the same as her mass on Earth.
questions.explain: Mass (the amount of matter) does not change. Her weight would be about one-sixth as much because the Moon's gravity is weaker.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which of these is the best conductor of heat?
questions.explain: Metals such as copper conduct heat well; that is why cookware uses metal. Wood, plastic, and air are insulators.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: An object will float in water if its density is:
choices: greater than the density of water.
less than the density of water.
exactly twice the density of water.
the same as the density of iron.
questions.explain: Objects less dense than water (1 g/cm³) float.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which type of electromagnetic wave carries the most energy?
questions.explain: Energy rises as wavelength shrinks. Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength and the highest energy.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: In a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the number of:
questions.explain: Electrons (−) balance protons (+), so a neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which of the following is a renewable energy source?
questions.explain: Wind is constantly replenished. Coal, oil, and natural gas are fossil fuels that took millions of years to form.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: The unit of electrical resistance is the:
questions.explain: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω). Volts measure voltage, amperes measure current, and watts measure power.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A 12-volt battery is connected to a 6-ohm resistor. How much current flows?
questions.explain: Ohm's law: I = E ÷ R = 12 ÷ 6 = 2 amps.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A 120-volt appliance draws 5 amps. How much power does it use?
questions.explain: P = E × I = 120 × 5 = 600 watts.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Three resistors of 10 Ω, 15 Ω, and 25 Ω are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
questions.explain: In series, resistances add: 10 + 15 + 25 = 50 Ω.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Two 8-ohm resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
questions.explain: Equal resistors in parallel: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 Ω. (Product over sum: 64 ÷ 16 = 4.)
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which material is the best electrical insulator?
questions.explain: Rubber blocks current. Copper and aluminum are conductors, and salt water conducts well.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: In a series circuit, which is the same through every component?
questions.explain: A series circuit has only one path, so the current is the same everywhere. The voltage divides among the parts.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which component allows current to flow in only one direction?
questions.explain: A diode is a one-way valve for current.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What does a step-down transformer do?
questions.explain: A step-down transformer has fewer turns on its secondary coil, so it lowers the voltage. Changing AC to DC is the job of a rectifier.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Household current in the United States is:
questions.explain: Standard U.S. outlets supply 120-volt alternating current at 60 hertz.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A resistor has the color bands brown, black, red. What is its resistance?
questions.explain: Brown = 1, black = 0, red = × 100. So 10 × 100 = 1,000 Ω.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What device protects a circuit by melting when the current gets too high?
questions.explain: A fuse contains a thin strip that melts and opens the circuit. A circuit breaker does the same job but can be reset.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which wire is thickest?
questions.explain: In the American Wire Gauge system, a smaller number means a thicker wire, so 10-gauge is thickest.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A capacitor is measured in:
questions.explain: Capacitance is measured in farads. Henrys measure inductance; hertz measure frequency.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Four 1.5-volt batteries are connected in series. What is the total voltage?
questions.explain: Batteries in series add their voltages: 4 × 1.5 = 6 volts.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: 0.5 amp flows through a 240-ohm resistor. What is the voltage across the resistor?
questions.explain: E = I × R = 0.5 × 240 = 120 volts.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A 60-watt lamp is connected to a 120-volt supply. How much current does it draw?
questions.explain: I = P ÷ E = 60 ÷ 120 = 0.5 amp.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A 6-ohm resistor and a 3-ohm resistor are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
questions.explain: Product over sum: (6 × 3) ÷ (6 + 3) = 18 ÷ 9 = 2 Ω — less than the smaller resistor, as it should be.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: In a parallel circuit, which quantity is the same across every branch?
questions.explain: Every branch connects directly across the source, so each has the same voltage. The current divides among the branches.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What happens to the total resistance of a parallel circuit when another branch is added?
questions.explain: Each new branch is another path for current, so total resistance decreases (and total current increases).
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which component stores energy in an electric field and blocks direct current?
questions.explain: A capacitor stores charge between its plates (an electric field) and blocks DC while passing AC. An inductor stores energy in a magnetic field.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A transformer has 1,000 turns on its primary coil and 100 turns on its secondary coil. If 120 volts AC is applied to the primary, what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explain: The voltage changes in proportion to the turns: 120 × (100 ÷ 1,000) = 12 volts. This is a step-down transformer.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A transistor is most commonly used as a(n):
questions.explain: A transistor uses a small base current to control a larger current, so it acts as an electronic switch or amplifier.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A resistor's bands are yellow, violet, orange. What is its value?
questions.explain: Yellow = 4, violet = 7, orange = × 1,000. 47 × 1,000 = 47,000 Ω (47 kΩ).
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What converts alternating current into direct current?
questions.explain: A rectifier (built from diodes) changes AC to DC. An inverter does the opposite.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: 250 milliamperes is equal to:
questions.explain: Milli- means one-thousandth: 250 ÷ 1,000 = 0.25 amp.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which instrument is used to measure electric current?
questions.explain: An ammeter measures current (amps). It is connected in series with the circuit.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a GFCI outlet?
choices: To raise the voltage for large appliances
To store energy during power outages
To cut off power quickly if current leaks to ground
questions.explain: A ground-fault circuit interrupter shuts off power within a fraction of a second if it senses current leaking to ground, which protects people from shock.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: 3 amps flow through a 10-ohm resistor. How much power does the resistor use?
questions.explain: P = I2 × R = 32 × 10 = 9 × 10 = 90 watts. (Or find E = 30 V first, then P = 30 × 3 = 90 W.)
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: In a series circuit with three lamps, one lamp burns out. What happens to the other two lamps?
questions.explain: A burned-out lamp opens the only path for current, so all the lamps go out. In a parallel circuit, the others would stay lit.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What is the correct order of the strokes in a four-stroke engine?
questions.explain: Intake, compression, power, exhaust — "suck, squeeze, bang, blow."
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: During which stroke do expanding gases push the piston down and produce power?
questions.explain: The mixture ignites at the top of the compression stroke, and the expanding gases drive the piston down on the power stroke — the only stroke that produces power.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which part converts the up-and-down motion of the pistons into rotating motion?
questions.explain: The crankshaft turns reciprocating (up-and-down) motion into rotation. The connecting rod links each piston to it.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A diesel engine ignites its fuel by using:
questions.explain: Diesel engines compress air until it is hot enough to ignite the injected fuel — compression ignition. They have no spark plugs.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What does the thermostat in the cooling system do?
choices: Controls coolant flow to the radiator based on engine temperature
Sets the temperature of the passenger cabin
questions.explain: The thermostat stays closed until the engine warms up, then opens to let coolant flow to the radiator. The water pump does the pumping.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which component recharges the battery while the engine is running?
questions.explain: The belt-driven alternator produces electricity to recharge the battery and run the electrical system.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: An engine cranks normally but will not start. What is the most likely cause?
choices: A lack of fuel or spark
questions.explain: If the engine cranks normally, the battery and starter are working. The problem is most likely that the engine is not getting fuel or spark.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Blue-gray smoke from the exhaust usually means the engine is:
questions.explain: Blue-gray smoke means oil is getting into the cylinders and burning, often from worn piston rings or valve seals. Black smoke means too much fuel; white smoke can mean coolant.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the catalytic converter?
questions.explain: The catalytic converter changes harmful gases into less harmful ones. The muffler reduces noise.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: In a disc brake, what squeezes the brake pads against the rotor?
questions.explain: The caliper clamps the pads against the rotor. Wheel cylinders and brake shoes belong to drum brakes.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A spongy, soft brake pedal most likely means:
choices: there is air in the brake lines.
the brake fluid reservoir is overfilled.
questions.explain: Air compresses, unlike brake fluid, so air in the hydraulic lines makes the pedal feel spongy. The fix is to bleed the brakes. Warped rotors cause a pulsating pedal.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What does the differential allow the drive wheels to do?
choices: Turn at different speeds when the vehicle goes around a corner
Disconnect from the engine while shifting
questions.explain: In a turn, the outside wheel travels farther than the inside wheel. The differential lets them turn at different speeds.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: In motor oil rated 10W-30, the "W" stands for:
questions.explain: The W stands for winter. The 10 describes how the oil flows when cold; the 30 describes its thickness at operating temperature.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: In an automatic transmission, which part takes the place of the clutch?
questions.explain: The torque converter, a fluid coupling, connects the engine to an automatic transmission.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which part of the suspension keeps a vehicle from continuing to bounce after hitting a bump?
questions.explain: Shock absorbers dampen spring motion. Springs absorb the bump but would keep bouncing without shocks.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: On a tire marked P215/65R15, what does the 15 mean?
questions.explain: The 15 is the rim diameter in inches. 215 is the width in millimeters, and 65 is the aspect ratio.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: When the key is turned, there is a clicking sound but the engine does not crank. What is the most likely cause?
choices: A weak battery or a poor battery connection
questions.explain: Clicking without cranking usually means the starter solenoid is trying to work but is not getting enough current — a weak battery or loose, corroded cables.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What does the PCV valve do?
choices: Routes crankcase vapors back into the engine to be burned
questions.explain: The positive crankcase ventilation valve sends gases that leak past the piston rings back into the intake so they are burned instead of released.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Rack-and-pinion is a type of:
questions.explain: In rack-and-pinion steering, a pinion gear on the steering shaft moves a toothed rack that turns the wheels.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A tire is worn on both outer edges but not in the center. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explain: An underinflated tire sags in the middle, so its outer edges carry the load and wear faster. Overinflation wears the center.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which saw is designed for cutting curves in thin wood?
questions.explain: A coping saw has a thin blade held in a U-shaped frame, so it can follow curves.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A ripsaw is used to cut wood:
questions.explain: A ripsaw cuts with (along) the grain. A crosscut saw cuts across it.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which tool would you use to check whether a shelf is perfectly horizontal?
questions.explain: A level shows whether a surface is horizontal (level) or vertical (plumb). A plumb bob shows only vertical.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A hacksaw is used mainly to cut:
questions.explain: The hacksaw has fine teeth in a tight frame for cutting metal and plastic pipe.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which hammer is used to shape metal and set rivets?
questions.explain: The rounded "peen" of a ball-peen hammer is used to shape metal and flatten rivets.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What is a torque wrench used for?
choices: Tightening fasteners to an exact specified tightness
questions.explain: A torque wrench measures how tightly a bolt is turned, so you can match the manufacturer's specification.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which pliers are best for gripping a small wire in a tight space?
questions.explain: Needle-nose pliers have long, thin jaws for small parts and tight spots.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A piece of lumber sold as a "2-by-4" actually measures about:
questions.explain: Lumber sizes are nominal. Drying and planing reduce a 2×4 to about 1½ × 3½ inches.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which nail is made to be driven below the surface of the wood and hidden?
questions.explain: A finishing nail has a tiny head that is set below the surface with a nail set, then covered.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A carriage bolt can be recognized by its:
questions.explain: The square neck under a carriage bolt's rounded head bites into wood so the bolt will not turn while the nut is tightened.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which tool cuts threads inside a drilled hole?
questions.explain: A tap cuts internal threads. A die cuts external threads on a rod.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: What is a countersink used for?
choices: Making a cone-shaped recess so a flat-head screw sits flush
Measuring the depth of a hole
questions.explain: A countersink shapes the top of a hole like a cone so a flat-head screw sits flush with the surface.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Brass is an alloy of:
questions.explain: Brass = copper + zinc. Bronze = copper + tin. Steel = iron + carbon.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Heating steel and then letting it cool slowly to make it softer is called:
questions.explain: Annealing (slow cooling) softens metal. Quenching (rapid cooling) hardens it.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which sandpaper is the finest?
questions.explain: The higher the grit number, the finer the paper. 220 is the finest choice here.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which welding process uses a continuously fed wire electrode and a shielding gas?
questions.explain: MIG welding feeds wire continuously through the gun while gas shields the weld. TIG uses a tungsten electrode that is not consumed.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Which tool is used to measure the gap of a spark plug?
questions.explain: A feeler gauge (or a wire gauge) measures small gaps such as spark plug and valve clearances.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: Concrete is made by mixing cement, water, sand, and:
questions.explain: Concrete = cement + water + sand + gravel. Mortar leaves out the gravel.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A Class B fire involves:
questions.explain: Class B fires involve flammable liquids. Class A is ordinary combustibles, Class C is electrical, and Class D is metals.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: A hacksaw blade should be installed with its teeth pointing:
questions.explain: A hacksaw cuts on the push stroke, so the teeth should point forward, away from the handle.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer.

questions.text: How much force (effort) is needed at the right end to balance the 120-pound load?
questions.explain: Effort × 6 = 120 × 2 → Effort × 6 = 240 → Effort = 40 lb. The longer effort arm gives an MA of 3.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of a second-class lever?
questions.explain: In a wheelbarrow, the wheel is the fulcrum, the load sits in the middle, and you lift the handles — load in the middle = second class. A seesaw and scissors are first class; tweezers are third class.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: How much effort is needed to lift the 200-pound load with this block and tackle?
questions.explain: Four rope sections hold up the movable block, so the MA is 4. Effort = 200 ÷ 4 = 50 lb.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.explain: Meshing gears alternate direction: A clockwise → B counterclockwise → C clockwise.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: A 20-tooth gear turning at 60 rpm drives a 40-tooth gear. How fast does the 40-tooth gear turn?
questions.explain: Teeth × rpm is equal for both gears: 20 × 60 = 40 × N, so N = 30 rpm. The bigger gear turns slower.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: A 400-pound barrel is rolled up a ramp 12 feet long to a platform 3 feet high. Ignoring friction, how much force is needed?
questions.explain: MA = length ÷ height = 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Effort = 400 ÷ 4 = 100 lb.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: A 50-pound force is applied to the small piston. How much force does the large piston exert?
questions.explain: Pressure = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 psi. That pressure acts on all 40 square inches of the large piston: 25 × 40 = 1,000 lb.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: Pulley A turns clockwise. Which way does pulley B turn?
choices: It depends on the pulley sizes
questions.explain: A crossed belt makes the pulleys turn in opposite directions, so B turns counterclockwise.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: A winch has a crank radius of 15 inches and an axle (drum) radius of 3 inches. How much force on the crank is needed to lift a 300-pound load?
questions.explain: MA = 15 ÷ 3 = 5. Effort = 300 ÷ 5 = 60 lb.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: A spring stretches 3 inches when a 12-pound weight hangs from it. How far will it stretch with a 20-pound weight?
questions.explain: The spring stretches 1 inch per 4 pounds (12 ÷ 3). 20 ÷ 4 = 5 inches.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: A 150-pound force is spread evenly over an area of 30 square inches. What is the pressure?
questions.explain: Pressure = force ÷ area = 150 ÷ 30 = 5 psi.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: Water flows through a pipe that narrows to half its width. Compared with the wide section, the water in the narrow section moves:
questions.explain: The same amount of water must pass through each section every second, so it must move faster where the pipe is narrow.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: How much of the 180-pound weight is supported by post A?
questions.explain: The weight is 3 feet from A and 9 feet from B. A's share = 180 × 912 = 135 lb (B carries 45 lb). The closer support carries more.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: Which change will make a pendulum swing more slowly?
choices: Pulling it back farther before releasing it
questions.explain: A pendulum's swing time depends on its length: a longer pendulum swings more slowly. The weight does not matter.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: Frames are built from rigid bars joined at the corners by pins. Which shape of frame best resists being pushed out of shape?
questions.explain: A triangle cannot change shape unless a side bends or breaks. Squares, rectangles, and hexagons can fold into slanted shapes at their pinned corners unless a diagonal brace is added — which turns them into triangles.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: In which class of lever is the effort applied between the fulcrum and the load?
questions.explain: Effort in the middle = third class (tweezers, a broom, your forearm).
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: How far from the fulcrum must the 120-pound person sit to balance the seesaw?
questions.explain: 80 × 6 = 120 × d → 480 = 120d → d = 4 ft. The heavier person sits closer.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: A 15-tooth driver gear turning clockwise at 200 rpm drives a 30-tooth idler gear, which drives a 45-tooth gear. How does the 45-tooth gear turn?
questions.explain: The idler does not change the overall ratio: 15 × 200 = 45 × N → N ≈ 67 rpm. Two meshes (driver → idler → output) bring the direction back to clockwise.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: A load hangs from a single movable pulley. To raise the load 3 feet, how much rope must be pulled?
questions.explain: A movable pulley has an MA of 2, so you pull twice the distance: 2 × 3 = 6 ft.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: A screw jack has a handle 14 inches long and a screw pitch of 14 inch. Ignoring friction, about how much force on the handle is needed to lift 3,520 pounds? (Use π ≈ 227.)
questions.explain: The handle travels 2 × 227 × 14 = 88 inches per turn while the load rises 14 inch. MA = 88 ÷ 0.25 = 352. Effort = 3,520 ÷ 352 = 10 lb.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.explain: The follower rises once for each lobe. This cam has two lobes, so the follower rises and falls twice per turn.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: The three tanks are filled with water to the same depth. At which tank is the water pressure on the bottom greatest?
choices: The pressure is the same in all three
questions.explain: Pressure in a liquid depends only on depth, not on the shape or size of the container. All three bottoms feel the same pressure.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: An object weighs 10 pounds. When it is completely underwater, it displaces 6 pounds of water. What will it do?
choices: Float with half of it above the water
Float with most of it above the water
Rise to the surface and stay there
questions.explain: The water can push up with at most 6 pounds, which is less than the object's 10-pound weight, so it sinks.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: The strip is made of brass bonded to steel. Brass expands more than steel when heated. When the strip is heated, which way will it bend?
questions.explain: The brass grows longer than the steel, so the brass ends up on the outside of the curve. The strip bends toward the steel — downward here.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.text: How much work is done in lifting a 50-pound box onto a shelf 4 feet high?
questions.explain: Work = force × distance = 50 × 4 = 200 ft-lb.
questions.instr: Choose the best answer. Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless the question says otherwise.

questions.explain: Diameter × rpm is equal: 4 × 900 = 12 × N → N = 300 rpm. The larger pulley turns more slowly.

questions.text: The wheel makes one complete turn. Which point travels the greatest distance?
questions.explain: Every point makes one turn, but the point farthest from the center — D, on the rim — travels around the biggest circle, so it travels farthest (and fastest).

questions.explain: D has the widest base and the lowest center of gravity. The tall, narrow object (A) tips most easily.

questions.text: Two identical springs hang side by side and together support a 20-pound weight. Each spring stretches 1 inch for every 5 pounds of load. How far does the weight move down?
questions.explain: Side-by-side (parallel) springs share the load: each carries 10 pounds and stretches 10 ÷ 5 = 2 inches.

questions.text: The basic unit of structure and function in all living things is the:
questions.explain: The cell is the basic unit of life. Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and atoms are not alive.

questions.text: Which organ filters wastes from the blood and produces urine?
questions.explain: The kidneys filter the blood and make urine. The liver processes nutrients and toxins and makes bile.

questions.text: Water vapor in the air turning into liquid droplets to form clouds is called:
questions.explain: Condensation is gas → liquid. Evaporation is the reverse; precipitation is rain or snow falling.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a renewable energy source?
questions.explain: Natural gas is a fossil fuel that takes millions of years to form. The others are constantly replenished.

questions.text: An animal that eats only plants is called a(n):
questions.explain: Herbivores eat plants. Carnivores eat meat, omnivores eat both, and decomposers break down dead matter.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula for table salt?
questions.explain: Table salt is sodium chloride, NaCl. KCl is potassium chloride, a salt substitute.

questions.text: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explain: Mars looks red because its surface contains iron oxide (rust).

questions.text: The force that resists motion between two surfaces that are touching is:
questions.explain: Friction opposes motion between surfaces in contact.

questions.text: Sound is produced by:
questions.explain: All sound comes from vibrations, which travel as waves through air, water, or solids.

questions.text: In the lungs, oxygen enters the blood through tiny air sacs called:
questions.explain: Gas exchange happens in the alveoli, which are surrounded by capillaries. The trachea and bronchi are airways; the diaphragm is a muscle.

questions.text: Which layer of Earth is the thinnest?
questions.explain: The crust is the thin outer shell. The mantle is the thickest layer.

questions.text: An atom that has gained or lost one or more electrons is called a(n):
questions.explain: An ion has an electrical charge because its electrons no longer equal its protons. Isotopes differ in neutrons.

questions.text: Which sugar do plants produce during photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis produces glucose (C6H12O6). Plants later build starch and cellulose from glucose.

questions.text: A scientist gives plants different amounts of fertilizer and measures how tall they grow. The amount of fertilizer is the:
questions.explain: The factor the scientist changes on purpose is the independent variable. Plant height, which is measured, is the dependent variable.

questions.text: Which type of rock forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure?
questions.explain: Metamorphic rock (such as marble or slate) forms under heat and pressure. Igneous rock forms from melted rock.

questions.text: A sailor earns $18.50 per hour. How much does she earn in a 40-hour week?
A recipe that serves 8 people uses 3 pounds of chicken. How many pounds are needed to serve 20 people?
questions.explain: 38 = x20 → 8x = 60 → x = 7.5 pounds.

questions.text: A store sells 3 notebooks for $4.20. At that rate, how much do 10 notebooks cost?
questions.explain: One notebook costs $4.20 ÷ 3 = $1.40. Ten cost $14.00.

questions.text: A tank holds 120 gallons of water. If 15% evaporates, how many gallons remain?
questions.explain: 15% of 120 = 18 gallons lost. 120 − 18 = 102 gallons remain (or 120 × 0.85).

questions.text: A convoy drives at 48 mph for 2.5 hours and then at 60 mph for 1.5 hours. How far does it travel in all?
questions.explain: First leg: 48 × 2.5 = 120 miles. Second leg: 60 × 1.5 = 90 miles. Total: 210 miles.

questions.text: A recruit ran 2.5 miles on Monday, 3.2 miles on Tuesday, 2.8 miles on Wednesday, and 3.5 miles on Thursday. What was her average distance per day?
questions.explain: Total: 2.5 + 3.2 + 2.8 + 3.5 = 12.0 miles. Average: 12 ÷ 4 = 3.0 miles.

questions.text: In a unit of 250 people, the ratio of officers to enlisted members is 1:9. How many officers are in the unit?
questions.explain: 1 + 9 = 10 parts. 250 ÷ 10 = 25 people per part, so there are 25 officers (and 225 enlisted).

questions.text: How much simple interest is earned on $3,000 at 5% per year for 18 months?
questions.explain: 18 months = 1.5 years. I = 3,000 × 0.05 × 1.5 = $225.

questions.text: One pump can fill a pool in 6 hours. A second pump can fill it in 12 hours. How long will it take both pumps working together?
questions.explain: Together: (6 × 12)(6 + 12) = 7218 = 4 hours. Check: 16 + 112 = 312 = 14 pool per hour.

questions.text: A shirt marked $40 is on sale for 25% off. At the register, another 10% is taken off the sale price. What is the final price?
questions.explain: Sale price: $40 × 0.75 = $30. Extra 10% off: $30 × 0.90 = $27. (Taking 35% off $40 would give $26 — the discounts do not simply add.)

questions.text: On a map, 12 inch represents 15 miles. How many miles do 414 inches represent?
questions.explain: 1 inch = 30 miles. 4.25 × 30 = 127.5 miles.

questions.text: A patio measures 18 feet by 12 feet. How many square tiles, each 6 inches on a side, are needed to cover it?
questions.explain: Each tile is 12 ft × 12 ft = 14 square foot. Patio area: 18 × 12 = 216 square feet. Tiles: 216 ÷ 14 = 864. (Or: 36 tiles along 18 ft × 24 tiles along 12 ft = 864.)

questions.text: Eight workers can paint a building in 15 days. Working at the same rate, how many days would 12 workers need?
questions.explain: The job is 8 × 15 = 120 worker-days. 120 ÷ 12 = 10 days.

questions.text: A bag holds 3 red, 5 blue, and 4 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is blue or green?
questions.explain: 5 + 4 = 9 of the 12 marbles are blue or green: 912 = 34.

questions.text: A father is 4 times as old as his son. In 20 years, the father will be twice as old as the son. How old is the son now?
questions.explain: Son = s, father = 4s. In 20 years: 4s + 20 = 2(s + 20) → 4s + 20 = 2s + 40 → s = 10. (Check: 40 and 10 now; 60 and 30 in 20 years.)

questions.text: Diligent most nearly means:
questions.explain: Diligent means hardworking and careful. Lazy is the opposite.

questions.text: Hazardous most nearly means:
questions.explain: Hazardous means full of hazards — dangerous.

questions.text: Obscure most nearly means:
questions.explain: Obscure means not clear or not well known. Of these choices, unclear fits. Obvious and well known are opposites.

questions.text: Concur most nearly means:
questions.explain: To concur is to agree (con- = together).

questions.text: The supply sergeant tried to expedite the order so the unit would have its gear before deployment. Expedite most nearly means:
questions.explain: The sergeant wanted the gear to arrive sooner, so expedite means speed up. Delay is the opposite.

questions.text: Sparse most nearly means:
questions.explain: Sparse means thinly scattered — few and far between (sparse vegetation). Crowded is the opposite.

questions.text: Lenient most nearly means:
questions.explain: A lenient judge is merciful and not strict.

questions.text: The tedious inventory took the whole weekend. Tedious most nearly means:
questions.explain: An inventory that drags on all weekend is boring and long.

questions.text: Pinnacle most nearly means:
questions.explain: A pinnacle is the highest point — a peak (the pinnacle of her career).

questions.text: Rudimentary most nearly means:
questions.explain: Rudimentary means basic or undeveloped (rudimentary first aid). Advanced is the opposite.

questions.text: After the long march, the soldiers were famished. Famished most nearly means:
questions.explain: Famished means extremely hungry — a natural result of a long march. It has nothing to do with fame.

questions.text: Inept most nearly means:
questions.explain: Inept (in- = not; ept from apt, skilled) means clumsy or incompetent.

questions.text: Abate most nearly means:
questions.explain: To abate is to lessen or die down (the storm abated).

questions.text: The inspector found the barracks in immaculate condition. Immaculate most nearly means:
questions.explain: Immaculate means perfectly clean, without a spot — exactly what an inspector hopes to see.

questions.text: Reticent most nearly means:
questions.explain: A reticent person is quiet and reserved, slow to share thoughts. Talkative is the opposite.

questions.text: The main point of the passage is that:
choices: soldiers should drink water only when they feel thirsty.
regular water breaks help prevent dehydration.
sweat helps keep the body cool.
questions.explain: The passage explains why thirst is unreliable and ends with its point: leaders schedule regular water breaks. The first choice contradicts the passage.

questions.text: According to the passage, thirst is a poor guide because:
choices: a person may already be dehydrated by the time he or she feels thirsty.
water is not always available during training.
sweat replaces the water the body loses.
people feel thirsty only at night.
questions.explain: The second sentence states it directly: "by the time a person feels thirsty, he or she may already be mildly dehydrated."

questions.text: According to the passage, the 1919 convoy:
choices: took about two months to cross the country.
traveled on the Interstate Highway System.
questions.explain: The passage says the trip "took about two months." The Interstate system did not exist until 1956.

questions.text: The passage suggests that Eisenhower supported a national highway system mainly because he believed it would:
questions.explain: The last sentence says he thought modern roads were "vital to national defense," based on seeing slow convoys and Germany's fast troop movements.

questions.text: What should be done before completing the leave form?
choices: Submit the form to the orderly room.
Discuss your plans with your supervisor.
questions.explain: The steps begin with "first discuss your plans with your supervisor"; "next" you complete the form.

questions.text: As used in the passage, "fragile" most nearly means:
questions.explain: Reefs are called fragile because they grow slowly and are sensitive to temperature changes — they are easily damaged.

questions.text: According to the passage, coral reefs are built by:
questions.explain: "The reefs are built by tiny animals called polyps."

questions.text: The author's main purpose is to:
choices: describe the most common reasons cars break down.
compare the prices of different flashlights.
explain how to use jumper cables.
persuade drivers to carry an emergency kit.
questions.explain: "Every driver should..." and the argument about cost versus trouble show that the author is persuading.

questions.text: Which conclusion is best supported by the passage?
choices: The new goggles will replace all of the old goggles this year.
The new goggles are heavier than the old ones.
The old goggles use fewer batteries than the new ones.
Most of the unit will keep using the older goggles for now.
questions.explain: Only "a few pairs" can be replaced this year, so most of the unit will still use the older model. The other choices contradict the passage.

questions.text: According to the passage, one advantage of the new goggles is that they:
questions.explain: The new goggles "weigh half as much as the older model." They cost more, not less.

questions.text: If 5x − 8 = 27, what is x?
questions.explain: 5x = 35, so x = 7.

questions.text: Simplify: 3(2x − 4) − 2(x − 5)
questions.explain: 6x − 12 − 2x + 10 = 4x − 2. Distributing −2 makes −2 × −5 = +10.

questions.text: What is the value of x2 − 4x + 7 when x = 3?
questions.explain: 9 − 12 + 7 = 4.

questions.text: Which expression is equal to (2x)3?
questions.explain: Cube both factors: 23 · x3 = 8x3.

questions.text: Factor: x2 − 36
questions.explain: A difference of squares: x2 − 62 = (x + 6)(x − 6).

questions.text: Solve: 2x3 = 12
questions.explain: Multiply both sides by 3: 2x = 36. Divide by 2: x = 18.

questions.text: An angle measures 35°. What is the measure of its supplement?
questions.explain: Supplementary angles total 180°: 180° − 35° = 145°. (55° is the complement.)

questions.text: What is the area of a triangle with a base of 14 and a height of 9?
questions.explain: A = 12 × 14 × 9 = 63. (126 forgets the 12.)

questions.text: What is the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 10?
questions.explain: C = πd = 10π. (25π would be the area, since the radius is 5.)

questions.text: What is 10% of 20% of 500?
If 3x = 81, what is x?
questions.explain: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81, so x = 4.

questions.text: What is the slope of the line 4x + 2y = 10?
questions.explain: Solve for y: 2y = −4x + 10 → y = −2x + 5. The slope is −2.

questions.text: What is the volume of a rectangular box that is 5 inches long, 4 inches wide, and 3 inches high?
questions.explain: V = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 cubic inches. (94 square inches is the surface area.)

questions.text: Which number is greatest?
questions.explain: Convert to decimals: 58 = 0.625, 35 = 0.6. The greatest is 58.

questions.text: Solve: x2 = 4x
questions.explain: x2 − 4x = 0 → x(x − 4) = 0 → x = 0 or x = 4. Dividing both sides by x would lose the solution x = 0.

questions.text: Electrical power is measured in:
questions.explain: Power is measured in watts. Volts measure voltage, ohms resistance, and amperes current.

questions.text: A 24-volt source is connected across an 8-ohm resistor. How much current flows?
questions.explain: I = E ÷ R = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 amps.

questions.text: Which of these is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explain: Copper is an excellent conductor. Glass, rubber, and porcelain are insulators.

questions.text: Resistors of 4 Ω, 6 Ω, and 10 Ω are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
questions.explain: Series resistances add: 4 + 6 + 10 = 20 Ω.

questions.text: Two 12-Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
questions.explain: Two equal resistors in parallel: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 Ω.

questions.text: A component that stores electric charge is a:
questions.explain: A capacitor stores charge on its plates.

questions.text: The symbol Ω stands for:
questions.explain: Ω (the Greek letter omega) is the symbol for ohms.

questions.text: If the voltage across a resistor doubles and the resistance stays the same, the current will:
questions.explain: From I = E ÷ R, current is proportional to voltage: double the voltage, double the current.

questions.text: A 1,500-watt heater runs on 120 volts. About how much current does it draw?
questions.explain: I = P ÷ E = 1,500 ÷ 120 = 12.5 amps.

questions.text: Which component is used to change alternating current into direct current?
questions.explain: A rectifier changes AC into DC. A transformer changes AC voltage but leaves it AC.

questions.text: Frequency is measured in:
questions.explain: Frequency (cycles per second) is measured in hertz. Henrys measure inductance; farads measure capacitance.

questions.text: In the resistor color code, which color stands for the digit 5?
questions.explain: Black 0, brown 1, red 2, orange 3, yellow 4, green 5, blue 6, violet 7, gray 8, white 9.

questions.text: A circuit breaker that trips again and again most likely means the circuit has:
choices: an overload or a short circuit.
questions.explain: Breakers trip when too much current flows — from too many devices (overload) or a short circuit.

questions.text: Current flows most easily through a material that has:
questions.explain: Lower resistance means easier current flow. Insulators have high resistance.

questions.text: A transformer's secondary coil has four times as many turns as its primary coil. The secondary voltage will be:
choices: the same as the primary voltage.
questions.explain: Voltage changes in proportion to the turns ratio. Four times the turns gives four times the voltage (a step-up transformer).

questions.text: What is the main job of the radiator?
choices: To heat the passenger cabin only
questions.explain: The radiator removes heat from the coolant so the engine does not overheat.

questions.text: Which part ignites the air–fuel mixture in a gasoline engine?
questions.explain: The spark plug fires to ignite the mixture. Glow plugs are used in diesel engines to help cold starts.

questions.text: The master cylinder is part of which system?
questions.explain: The master cylinder turns brake-pedal force into hydraulic pressure for the brakes.

questions.text: What does the muffler do?
choices: Cleans harmful gases from the exhaust
questions.explain: The muffler quiets the exhaust. Cleaning harmful gases is the catalytic converter's job.

questions.text: The battery warning light comes on while a car is being driven. The most likely problem is with the:
questions.explain: The battery light means the battery is not being charged — usually an alternator problem or a loose or broken belt.

questions.text: Universal joints (U-joints) are found on the:
questions.explain: U-joints at each end of the driveshaft let it turn while its angle changes as the suspension moves.

questions.text: The crankshaft turns the camshaft by means of the:
questions.explain: The timing belt or chain keeps the camshaft (valves) in step with the crankshaft (pistons).

questions.text: Black smoke from the exhaust usually means the engine is:
questions.explain: Black smoke means a rich mixture — too much fuel. Blue-gray smoke means burning oil; white smoke can mean coolant.

questions.text: Which tool is used to check an engine's compression?
questions.explain: A compression gauge screws into a spark plug hole and measures the pressure in each cylinder.

questions.text: Front-wheel-drive vehicles use CV joints so that the front wheels can:
choices: steer while still receiving power from the engine.
questions.explain: Constant velocity joints let the front wheels steer and drive at the same time.

questions.text: Which tool is best for driving common nails?
questions.explain: A claw hammer is designed for driving (and pulling) nails. A ball-peen hammer is for metalworking.

questions.text: What is a bench vise used for?
choices: Holding work securely while you cut, file, or drill it
questions.explain: A vise clamps work firmly to the bench.

questions.text: Which saw is used with a miter box to make accurate straight cuts?
questions.explain: The backsaw has a stiff spine that keeps it straight in a miter box.

questions.text: A heavy screw with a hex head that is turned into wood with a wrench is a:
questions.explain: A lag screw (lag bolt) has a hex head and coarse threads for wood.

questions.text: Which tool should be used to cut sheet metal?
questions.explain: Tin snips cut sheet metal like heavy-duty scissors.

questions.text: A carpenter's level is used to check whether a surface is:
questions.explain: A level shows whether something is perfectly horizontal or vertical.

questions.text: Which tool removes the sharp burr from the inside of a pipe after it has been cut?
questions.explain: A reamer cleans and smooths the inside edge of a cut pipe.

questions.text: Which sandpaper grit should be used first on a rough board?
questions.explain: Start with a coarse (low-number) grit such as 60, then move to finer grits.

questions.text: An Allen wrench is used on screws that have:
choices: a square head for pipe fittings.
questions.explain: An Allen (hex) key fits screws with a hexagonal socket.

questions.text: Which joint is commonly used to join drawer sides because its interlocking parts make it very strong?
questions.explain: The fan-shaped tails and pins of a dovetail joint lock together and resist being pulled apart.

questions.text: How much effort is needed to balance the load?
questions.explain: Effort × 9 = 90 × 3 → Effort × 9 = 270 → Effort = 30 lb.
questions.instr: Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless a question says otherwise.

questions.text: A 30-tooth gear turning at 40 rpm drives a 10-tooth gear. How fast does the 10-tooth gear turn?
questions.explain: 30 × 40 = 10 × N → N = 120 rpm. The smaller gear turns faster.
questions.instr: Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless a question says otherwise.

questions.text: A single movable pulley is used to lift a 150-pound load. How much effort is needed?
questions.explain: A movable pulley has an MA of 2: 150 ÷ 2 = 75 lb.
questions.instr: Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless a question says otherwise.

questions.text: Pulley A turns clockwise. Which way does pulley B turn?
questions.explain: With an open (uncrossed) belt, both pulleys turn in the same direction.
questions.instr: Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless a question says otherwise.

questions.text: A 600-pound crate is pushed up a ramp 15 feet long to a dock 5 feet high. How much force is needed?
questions.explain: MA = 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Effort = 600 ÷ 3 = 200 lb.
questions.instr: Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless a question says otherwise.

questions.text: In a hydraulic jack, a 30-pound force is applied to a piston with an area of 1 square inch. The large piston has an area of 25 square inches. How much force does the large piston exert?
questions.explain: Pressure = 30 ÷ 1 = 30 psi. Force on large piston = 30 × 25 = 750 lb.
questions.instr: Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless a question says otherwise.

questions.text: Which of these tools works on the wheel-and-axle principle?
questions.explain: A screwdriver handle (the wheel) turns a narrow shaft (the axle), multiplying your turning force.
questions.instr: Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless a question says otherwise.

questions.explain: Directions alternate: 1 clockwise, 2 counterclockwise, 3 clockwise, 4 counterclockwise.
questions.instr: Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless a question says otherwise.

questions.text: A 5-pound weight stretches a spring 2 inches. How much weight would stretch it 7 inches?
questions.explain: The spring stretches 1 inch per 2.5 pounds. 7 × 2.5 = 17.5 lb.
questions.instr: Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless a question says otherwise.

questions.text: How much of the 200-pound load does support A carry?
questions.explain: The load is 4 ft from A and 6 ft from B. A's share = 200 × 610 = 120 lb (B carries 80 lb). The nearer support carries more.
questions.instr: Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless a question says otherwise.

questions.text: At which point is the water pressure greatest?
questions.explain: Water pressure increases with depth. Point D is the deepest.
questions.instr: Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless a question says otherwise.

questions.text: Which wedge would split a log with the least force?
choices: A wedge with a rounded tip
A wedge that is wider at the tip than at the back
questions.explain: A long, thin wedge has the greatest mechanical advantage, like a gentle ramp.
questions.instr: Ignore friction and the weight of levers, ropes, and pulleys unless a question says otherwise.

questions.text: A bolt has 10 threads per inch. How many turns are needed to move it 1.5 inches?
